FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 April 1989, 
after the draft finalized by the Metal Forming Machines and Tools Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

This standard based on DIN 9859 ( Part 1 ) : 1963 'Shanks — Survey, general dimensions', issued 
by the Deutsches Institut fur Normung ( DIN ). This part is one of a series of standards on press 
working tools. Other parts are as follows: 

Press working tools — shanks 
Shanks to suit riveting 
Shanks with screwed shaft 
Shanks with neck and collar 
Shanks with round flanges ( under preparation ) 
Shanks with rectangular flanges ( under preparation ) 
Shanks with screwed shaft and collar ( under preparation )

IS 12665 ( Part 1) : 1989 



Indian Standard 



PRESS WORKING TOOLS — SHANKS 

PART I GENERAL DIMENSIONS AND SURVEY 

1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) covers general dimensions and survey of various types of shanks used for 
connecting the top tool holder to the press ram to achieve rigid connection. 

2 TYPES 

2.1 The shanks shall be of the following types:

NOTES 

1 Shanks shown with notch and groove are safer due to facility for clamping with a set screw at notch or groove 
to prevent falling. 

2 Shanks shown with plain, notch and groove are integral with flanges and are provided with a radius r 2 . 

3 Shanks of sizes di=% to 16 mm are suitable for very small presses only. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. * 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS iS~a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
urade designations.. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, wheji necessary and amendments, if an\, 
are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession 
of the latest amendments x>r edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving 
the following reference : 

Doc: No. EDC72(46'I6)
